claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure consisting of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Introducing nano-scale precipitates within the lamellar colonies can overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness.
Introducing nano-scale precipitates can retain or increase the alloy's strength.
Nano-scale precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation movement.
Obstruction of dislocation movement by nano-scale precipitates reduces dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries decreases local stress concentrations.
Reducing local stress concentrations decreases microcracking during straining.
Reducing local stress concentrations and microcracking decreases catastrophic damage during straining.
The precipitate-modified alloy will exhibit improved tensile ductility relative to the untreated alloy.
The precipitate-modified alloy will retain or exceed the tensile strength of the untreated alloy.
The predicted behavior applies under room-temperature uniaxial tensile testing.
The effectiveness of the precipitates may depend on their size, distribution, and composition.
A controlled comparison of untreated and precipitate-modified alloys under room-temperature uniaxial tension can test the hypothesis.
